Arsenal dominated every metric against a promoted Coventry team that looked, frankly, a little spooked by their first sight of that fresh Everest.Graphic showing teams with less of the ball won an unusually high proportion of Premier League games in matchweek oneSo, a tiny sample size. It may mean absolutely nothing. It could get flipped on its head before we hit September. Also, it is important to note that pure possession stats have rarely dictated with any certainty who will win a game. The top teams always tend to have most of the ball, thus skewing the overall stats.Otherwise, possession has been a far less reliable guide to victory than, say, expected goals, which speaks clearly to the effectiveness of a system. Whereas simply keeping the ball is often a sign of the opposite of good health, of football as a collective anxiety attack, out there playing with your worry beads, tramping a horseshoe shape into the grass while your opponents mass for the decisive blitzkrieg.Quick GuidePlay our football trivia game, On the ballShowThe Guardian'sdaily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues?Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.But it wasn’t just the possession numbers that were notable this weekend. The rhythms of the matches were striking. All three Sunday games featured nine or 10 substitutes in the last 40 minutes or so, and a sense of two separate halves, of finishers brought into play, of a broken, episodic tactical to‑and‑fro in response to shifts in the scoreline and the flow. The World Cup also had that pattern. Maybe this is what football is now.Mainly there was a striking level of targeted physicality, rehearsed blitz-transitions, groups of players running suddenly forward quickly in formation at certain triggering events. Anthony Elanga’s opener for Newcastle captured this best: 12 seconds, two passes, 70 metres covered in a single perfectly straight line, no off‑the‑cuff inventions or what you might call conventional “creativity”, but a perfect moment of planned collective intelligence and breathtaking athleticism.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThis was the pattern elsewhere too, games defined by rapid breaks, by powerful players sourced for their ability to win duels and to carry the ball, and a weekend that felt like another ratcheting up in the Premier League’s journey into hyper‑physicality.Graphic showing sprints and distance covered beat possession for correlation with winning in match week oneIsn’t it a trend? Is this the next stage in the league’s narrow but furiously intense evolution? There are several managers in new jobs who have reputations for the game of sprints, blitz‑ball: most notably Matthias Jaissle at Newcastle and Roberto De Zerbi at what was, on Saturday, the least De Zerbi‑ish of Spurs, a Spurs that seemed to have absorbed only the mouse part – play dead, hide, roll over – of that fast‑breaking cat‑and‑mouse football.There are two things worth saying about this. This is not a rejection of Guardiolaism and positional play. Keeping the ball was always about preparing for the moments when you don’t have it. Guardiola’s later Manchester City team would often win by direct means.But pure possession can also be boringly risk-averse, a kind of footballing atrophy where everyone just sits quivering on the touchline like a swarm of beached jellyfish at dusk. The spectacle is more gripping when the emphasis is on those transitions either side of the passing patterns.More specifically, it is also an interesting development for Pep’s successor at City, Enzo Maresca, Coolio to his Tupac, whose methods are still very much pure Pep origins, based in control of the ball and rigid positionism, like the last soldier still fighting the second world war from inside a bush on Iwo Jima in 1976.View image in fullscreenNewcastle’s Anthony Elanga celebrates his superb strike against Liverpool.Photograph: Simon Davies/ProSports/ShutterstockIs Maresca ready for this? Is he even ahead of it? He gave a televised interview at the weekend where he spoke about the tension between control and risk, possession and creativity, and where he defined players being encouraged to run into unexpected positions as “chaos”. On Monday morning there were headlines describing the Premier League weekend in those terms. But this isn’t chaos. We’ve seen chaos. We’ve seen attackshipson fire off the shoulder of Orion, jinking wingers,dogs of war, hitting the space, Lee Chapman, Rod Wallace and Eric Cantona making heavy metal music with two bass guitars and anantiqueviola. You want chaos. We can give you chaos.What the Premier League brought at the weekend, the quick breaks, the freedom to attack at selected moments, was more a kind of hyper-managed shock and awe, targeted speed and physicality born out of calculated risk, numbers, data, heavy briefings.It was also exciting to watch, which is no bad thing in the world’s most tightly contested, space‑averse league. No doubt there will be tightening, a reaction to the reaction, instant counter‑moves and contingency planning. August can also be odd and silly season-ish, the dog days of a World Cup summer. But it did at times feel as if we were in a post‑something moment. If not quite post‑Pep, whose influence will continue to loom, a tactical Machiavelli with plenty of tapes still left in the vault.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeaguePep GuardiolaManchester CityanalysisShareReuse this content

title: San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York pleads no contest after arrest at Ohio trailer park | San Francisco 49ers | The Guardian
description: The San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York has pleaded no contest to two criminal charges after being arrested in Ohio over the weekend
Author: Tom Lutz
Headline: The San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York has pleaded no contest to two criminal charges after being arrested in Ohio over the weekend
Content: Jed York also owns a stake in Leeds United.Photograph: Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenJed York also owns a stake in Leeds United.Photograph: Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty ImagesSan Francisco 49ersSan Francisco 49ers owner Jed York pleads no contest after arrest at Ohio trailer park46-year-old charged with possessing criminal toolsYork fined and sentenced to two days in jail49ers CEO also owns stake in Leeds UnitedTom LutzMon 24 Aug 2026 12.21 EDTLast modified on Mon 24 Aug 2026 16.26 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTheSan Francisco 49ersowner Jed York has pleaded no contest to two criminal charges after being arrested at an Ohio trailer park over the weekend.KRON4 News in San Franciscoreported that York was initially arrested on suspicion of engaging in prostitution but that count was amended to a charge of disorderly conduct. He was also charged with possessing criminal tools.A no contest plea is not an admission of guilt but the defendant in question does accept the punishment for the alleged crimes in question. York was sentenced to a day in jail for each count to be served concurrently and was released on Monday morning. He was also fined a total of $1,150 and ordered to complete an online course. The arrest report does not specify what the criminal tools were in York’s case.According to the New York Post, court documents say York responded to an advert on a website and “arranged to have sexual activity with [a] female in exchange for $140.” York was arrested later arrested at a trailer park in East Palestine, Ohio, on Sunday morning. The East Palestine Police Department and the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force were involved in the arrest. York, 46, was born and raised in Youngstown, a 30-minute drive from East Palestine and still has a home in the area.York is the nephew of former 49ers majority owner Edward J DeBartolo Jr. York took day to day control of the 49ers in 2008 when he became the team’s CEO. After acquiring his mother’s shares, he became the team’s principal owner in 2024.“As this is a legal matter, which has been resolved, we will not be providing any further comment at this time,” the 49ers said in a statement. TheNFLsaid in a statement that it is “aware of the matter which will be reviewed under the personal conduct policy.”Since York took over as CEO, the 49ers have reached three Super Bowls but lost each time.He also owns stakes in the Premier League’sLeeds Unitedand Scotland’s Rangers through 49ers Enterprises. He filed for divorce from his wife, Danielle, in May.Explore more on these topicsSan Francisco 49ersNFLSan FranciscoWest CoastUS sportsLeeds UnitedRangersnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘Enough is enough’: players pile pressure on under-fire Gianni Infantino to resign | Gianni Infantino | The Guardian
description: A group of influential current and former footballers have added to the pressure on Gianni Infantino by calling for change at the top of Fifa
Author: Nick Ames
Headline: A group of influential current and former footballers have added to the pressure on Gianni Infantino by calling for change at the top of Fifa
Content: Gianni Infantino was at a youth tournament in the Dominican Republic on Saturday in an attempt to smooth relations with smaller Caribbean member associations on whose support his Fifa fate may hinge.Photograph: Teresa Suárez/ReutersView image in fullscreenGianni Infantino was at a youth tournament in the Dominican Republic on Saturday in an attempt to smooth relations with smaller Caribbean member associations on whose support his Fifa fate may hinge.Photograph: Teresa Suárez/ReutersGianni Infantino‘Enough is enough’: players pile pressure on under-fire Gianni Infantino to resignPresident accused by ‘Fifa Legends’ of being power hungrySamuel Eto’o claims chief has not ‘done anything wrong’Nick AmesMon 24 Aug 2026 14.19 EDTLast modified on Mon 24 Aug 2026 18.38 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleA group of influential current and former footballers have added to the pressure onGianni Infantinoby calling for change at the top of Fifa, saying “enough is enough” in a statement shared widely across social media.The intervention is particularly significant given some of those behind its circulation have undertaken ambassadorial activities forFifaas part of its “Fifa Legends” programme. Among them is the former Manchester United and Arsenal defender Mikaël Silvestre, who also sits on the governing body’s 16-member players’ voice panel designed to assist with anti-racism initiatives.Infantino angers Concacaf nations by hijacking meeting in CaribbeanRead moreOthers to have shared the statement include the England defender Lucy Bronze, the former England keeper David James and the France 1998 World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit. More signatories are expected to follow in a concerted reaction to Infantino’s ill-fated attempt tosell stakes in the World Cup.“We share the exact same concerns as the millions of fans around the world,” part of the statement read. “Like them, we have watched the game we love drift away from its core values under Fifa’s current leadership. For too long, we’ve seen major decisions taken without players being consulted or considered, and without any regard for the fans who sustain the sport.Quick GuidePlay our football trivia game, On the ballShowThe Guardian'sdaily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues?Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.“Change is necessary. Power has blurred the current leadership’s ability to distinguish between its own interests and what is best for football. Recent events have made silence impossible. Enough is enough.”The group called for efforts to “reshape the future of our sport”, adding: “There are good people within Fifa who want to rebuild trust, but a new era requires a structured change: a real, direct say for players and fans in how football is run. Those who step on to the pitch and those who sit in the stands deserve a genuine voice to help reshape football’s future together.”Infantino has resisted calls to resign and spent Saturday at ayouth tournament in the Dominican Republic, attempting to smooth relations with some of the smaller Caribbean member associations on whose support his fate may hinge.One former player with a different perspective on Infantino is the former Real Madrid, Barcelona and Chelsea striker Samuel Eto’o, who is president of the Cameroonian football federation. In an interview with CNN, Eto’o said Infantino had not committed any missteps and called for the Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme to be put back on the table if Infantino is re-elected next March. He said the money from FFE would “reset the balance of power” in football and ensure African countries avoided losing top players to other national teams.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“I don’t think that [Infantino] has done anything wrong,” he said. “All of this has happened because there’s an election coming out, that’s all there is.“I want to see all of my colleagues, all of the presidents, re-reading the project. After president Infantino is re-elected, we will have the strength to ask for this project to be put back on the table for discussion. I remain convinced that, if there is a democratic vote, this project will be adopted because it’s good for the majority.”Explore more on these topicsGianni InfantinoFifaFootball politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: The men claiming to defend women’s sports are throwing sex toys at female athletes | WNBA | The Guardian
description: The WNBA has attracted grifters who care little for basketball – and whose latest stunt exposes the hollowness of their supposed concern
Author: Dave Schilling
Headline: The WNBA has attracted grifters who care little for basketball – and whose latest stunt exposes the hollowness of their supposed concern
Content: Chicago Sky’s game against the Golden State Valkyries last week was disrupted.Photograph: Michael Reaves/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenChicago Sky’s game against the Golden State Valkyries last week was disrupted.Photograph: Michael Reaves/Getty ImagesWNBAThe men claiming to defend women’s sports are throwing sex toys at female athletesThe WNBA has attracted grifters who care little for basketball – and whose latest stunt exposes the hollowness of their supposed concernDave SchillingMon 24 Aug 2026 05.00 EDTLast modified on Mon 24 Aug 2026 05.02 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIregret to inform you that yet another dildo has hit a WNBA court. The Chicago Sky v Golden State Valkyries game was sullied bysex toys being chucked on to the playing surface on Friday. Aren’t we tired of all this yet? Toparaphrase the Sky’s Natasha Cloud, it takes a lot of effort to bother with such a juvenile act.This is yet another controversy for theWNBA, a league that up until a few years ago, most media observers ignored. The WNBA is full of incredibly talented players and has a rich history, but most sports fans treated all but ignored it for the majority of its 30-year existence. But when Caitlin Clark went pro, the league surged. Ratings, attendance, and interest exploded. But not all attention is good attention.Buzzer-beaters and besties: the rivalries and friendships that make the WNBARead moreClark has been polarizing from the start, owing to the fact that she’s a white superstar in a league that has historically been dominated by Black players. That alone makes her a prime candidatefor culture warriors to weigh in. But now, the level of debate around the league has somehow become worse. Clark’s teammate, Sophie Cunningham, chose this fraught moment to declare she’sagainst trans women playing in girls’ and women’s sports. Never mind that the league has never had a trans player assigned male at birth and this is all just a hypothetical scenario she’s concerned about. Cunningham is better at getting attention thanscoring points.Protests outside Fever gamesare often covered on the news more than the games inside the arena, which is hardly the kind of attention the WNBA has been looking for. A league that has long prided itself on its LGBTQ fans and players is now at the center of transphobic controversy. And then, it started raining dildos.The Sky-Valkyries game is not the first time sex toys have been thrown on to the court at a WNBA game – the dismal incidents started last season. It’s not even theonly league where this has happened. Regardless, the timing is pointed. The WNBA is not just a sports league – it’s also a furious petri dish for the opinions of people who often don’t even like women’s basketball. Agroup of crypto traders took responsibilityfor previous incidents and the most recent one in Chicago, declaring their support for Cunningham’s stance against trans women playing in the WNBA (which again, has not happened). You’d think they’d have come up with a new stunt, but apparently, good ideas are in short supply these days (they tried the same stunt last season to promote a meme coin, and there appears to be plenty of self-promotion behind these recent ones too). And if the group – and many of the anti-trans brigade who have descended on the WNBA – truly cared about women’s sports, perhaps funding scholarships and teams for young female athletes would be a more constructive way of going about it.With outlets like Fox News forced to cover the league and hucksters like ex-NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom coming outto glom onto the controversy, the WNBA seems to be drowning in the kind of press no one wants. There’s along history of athletes speaking up about their political and cultural opinions, but this seems especially dire when a women’s basketball player is actively speaking out against a community that has historically supported the sport. The WNBA finds itself in a culture war ignited by one of its own players, and the absurd spectacle of young men throwing sex toys at female athletes in the name of protecting women’s sports is just another front in that conflict. The “stick to sports” mantra that was so popular during the first Trump administration has become a punchline every time a dildo gets thrown on a basketball court.The sex toy incidents are just the physical manifestation of what Cunningham has done to her league – a needless plea for attention that serves no one but the person making the fuss. This was not a subject the WNBA was dealing with until she said something. It’s now something the WNBA can’t get away from. If women’s basketball is to maintain its recent growth it needs to continue producing stars like Clark, four-time MVP A’ja Wilson andthe ridiculously talented Olivia Miles. What it doesn’t need is players who court controversy for their own personal gain. Cunningham was barely on most fans’ radars until shebecame a meme, an honor usually reserved for such cultural luminaries as The Rizzler and the Real Housewives of Beverly Hills. Good for her, I guess. No doubt her post-career podcast will be thrilling. But where does she leave the WNBA? Drowning in the aftermath of childish pranks, it seems.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Weekly for the 2026 WNBA seasonSign up toWNBA 30A limited run women’s basketball newsletter dedicated to the league’s historic 30th season.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionNo doubt there will be further moronic stunts this season, especially during the high visibility period of the WNBA playoffs and finals. The league can’t stipulate the terms of players’ speech. It can only ban those young men who disrupt games (and it is only young men who have been apprehended for the stunts so far), although there seems to be an endless supply of them. If the WNBA is going to sustain itself and bring in more genuine fans (as opposed to people solely interested in the league because they want to make a political point), it will need to address all of this in some meaningful way. The bond it has built with many of the LGBTQ fans who have helped sustain and build the league is being torched, with the help of one of its own players. And now outside agitators have joined the party.Explore more on these topicsWNBABasketballUS sportsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Vuelta a España: giant hail forces stage three abandonment in Pyrenees | Vuelta a España | The Guardian
description: A torrential hailstorm in ⁠the French Pyrenees forced the ⁠abandonment of ⁠the ​third stage of the Vuelta a ⁠España
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: A torrential hailstorm in ⁠the French Pyrenees forced the ⁠abandonment of ⁠the ​third stage of the Vuelta a ⁠España
Content: Wout van Aert of Team Visma heads to a hotel for cover after the abandonment of stage three.Photograph: Tim de Waele/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenWout van Aert of Team Visma heads to a hotel for cover after the abandonment of stage three.Photograph: Tim de Waele/Getty ImagesVuelta a EspañaVuelta a España: giant hail forces stage three abandonment in PyreneesHuge hailstones prompt organisers to act 15km from endRiders seen heading into hotel on route to take coverReutersMon 24 Aug 2026 13.21 EDTFirst published on Mon 24 Aug 2026 11.56 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleA torrential hailstorm in the French Pyrenees forced the abandonment of the ⁠third stage of theVuelta a Españaon Monday.With 15 kilometres (9.32 miles) remaining of the 174km route ⁠from Gruissan to Font-Romeu, the ​skies darkened as the peloton neared the top of the Col de Mont-Louis and huge hailstones began ⁠bouncing off the tarmac and pelting the riders.Mats Wenzel (Kern Pharma) and Lorenzo Fortunato (XDS Astana) were 25 seconds ahead ⁠of the peloton when the elements intervened as the race leader and favourite ​Tadej Pogacar was seen indicating ‌to the peloton ‌to pull off the course.View image in fullscreenA view of the finish line following the stage cancellation.Photograph: Alexander Hassenstein/Getty ImagesBedraggled riders were then seen getting off their ‌bikes and shuffling into a hotel for shelter, leaving fans frustrated at the finish where thick layers of hail blanketed the road.“For the security of the riders, stage three has been cancelled due to hail and severe weather,” race organisers said shortly afterwards. “There will be no winner and no podium ceremony.”Pogacar (UAE Emirates-XRG) retained his overall lead of nine seconds from the Belgian rider ‌Wout van Aert (Dutch Visma-Lease a Bike) with the British rider Matt Brennan 10sec back.Earlier it had been warm and sunny ​on the flat approaches to the mountainous finish with no sign of the chaos to come as a five-man breakaway group stayed out ahead.Quick GuideHow do I sign up for sport breaking news alerts?ShowIn the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from theiOS App Storeon iPhone or theGoogle Play storeon Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Pogacar, bidding to complete his Grand Tour collection by winning the Vuelta ⁠for the first time, was always near the front of ​the pack with ​the Slovenian’s team setting the pace.His expected challenge for the stage victory fell foul ​of the ‌weather in an ​anticlimactic finish. Pogacar ​will get his chance to underline his superiority again on Tuesday, though, with stage four featuring three first-category climbs as the race starts and finishes in Andorra la Vella.Explore more on these topicsVuelta a EspañaTadej PogacarCyclingSpainEuropenewsShareReuse this content

title: Chelsea’s front three dazzle as they edge out Fulham in derby thriller | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Chelsea’s front three of João Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer were all on target as they began the Xabi Alonso era with a 3-2 win at Fulham
Author: Jacob Steinberg
Headline: Chelsea’s front three of João Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer were all on target as they began the Xabi Alonso era with a 3-2 win at Fulham
Content: Chelsea's Cole Palmer celebrates scoring his side's third goal with João Pedro (left) and Morgan Rogers.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianView image in fullscreenChelsea's Cole Palmer celebrates scoring his side's third goal with João Pedro (left) and Morgan Rogers.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianPremier LeagueChelsea’s front three dazzle as they edge out Fulham in derby thrillerJacob Steinbergat Craven CottageMon 24 Aug 2026 17.05 EDTLast modified on Mon 24 Aug 2026 19.05 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GooglePerhaps there will come a time when Xabi Alonso has taughtChelseahow to master the art of game management. This is a team still to learn how to grind. Equally it is a team capable of hurting anyone, and although Alonso’s first outing as Chelsea’s manager featured plenty of terrible defending it also provided confirmation that life will never be dull with a front three of Cole Palmer, João Pedro and Morgan Rogers.No wonder Maxence Lacroix wanted to join in the fun. The £52m centre‑back marked his debut with a thrilling assist, storming forward to make Rogers’s first goal since his £117m move from Aston Villa. João Pedro was no less effective as the No 9, while the biggest positive for Alonso had to be Palmer looking rested, dangerous and determined to prove a point after his injury woes last season led to him being left out of England’s World Cup squad.Glaring weakness in goal remains but early signs Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea should be fun | Jonathan WilsonRead moreKeep playing this well and Thomas Tuchel will surely name Palmer alongside Rogers for the Nations League games next month. Chelsea’s two No 10s both got to do the “ice cold” celebration and their combinations with João Pedro should have been enough to ensure this 3-2 win againstFulhamwas less stressful.There were reminders that Chelsea have much to improve if they want to challenge for the title. Their defending left much to be desired, even with the towering Lacroix in the middle of the back three, and Robert Sánchez’s feeble attempt to stop Josh King from scoring Fulham’s first goal bolsters the argument that Chelsea need a new No 1.Alonso refused to single out Sánchez. The Spaniard said it was down to the team to defend better as a collective, but he also argued that his players delivered a mature performance. It was thePremier Leagueat its best – wild, relentless, moments of high class followed by inexplicable mistakes – and despite losing Fulham could feel there is life after Marco Silva.View image in fullscreenCole Palmer scores Chelsea’s third goal in their win at Fulham.Photograph: Ryan Pierse/Getty ImagesAlvaro Arbeloa, whose friendship with Alonso goes back almost two decades, saw intensity and quality from Fulham. The 19-year-old King sparkled as the No 10. Oscar Bobb was bright on the right and it was easy to see why Arbeloa has brought César Palacios and Gonzalo García with him from Madrid. Palacios offered smooth touches in midfield and Arebloa knew it was important for García to score on his debut in attack.Yet while Fulham have lowered the age of their squad they were let down by naive defending. Chelsea’s first goal, scored after 31 seconds, was a catastrophe. A long ball floated through the middle and with Jorge Cuenca out of position in central defence Palmer exacted punishment with a flick to release João Pedro, who built on his scorching pre-season form by dinking a finish over Bernd Leno.It is hard to judge Arbeloa’s level given his managerial experience is limited to stepping in at Madrid after Alonso’s firing last season. Fulham played their part in a pulsating first half, though, and were level when King’s shot from a tight angle exposed Sánchez’s positioning.Chelsea were without Moisés Caicedo in midfield, where there was a rare start for Roméo Lavia alongside Reece James, and they lacked control before half-time. Marco Palestra was also unable to make his debut because of a minor knock. Malo Gusto and Jorrel Hato seemed cautious picks as the wing-backs in the 3-4-2-1 system Alonso used when winning the Bundesliga with Bayer Leverkusen in 2024.It is a work in progress. Composure eluded Chelsea, typified by Levi Colwill and Lavia picking up bookings inside the first 12 minutes. Fulham had chances to lead but Josh Acheampong denied Garceia.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenJosh King scores Fulham’s first goal.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianChelsea were a handful at the other end. Lavia threatened and João Pedro volleyed wide from a Palmer cross. Rogers pressed, harried and got his goal. Palmer started the move, finding the overlapping Lacroix, who beat a weak challenge and cut the ball back for Rogers to score.Fulham took a lot of risks on and off the ball. They were too open at times and it was 3-1 at the start of the second half. João Pedro beat a faulty offside and found Palmer, who deceived Leno by giving the goalkeeper the eyes before nutmegging him with a clever finish.That should have enough but Fulham had hope when Colwill misjudged a long ball, Sánchez spilled Timothy Castagne’s shot and García headed in the rebound.Quick GuidePlay our football trivia game, On the ballShowThe Guardian'sdaily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues?Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Seeking order, Alonso made changes. A cramping Lavia made way for Enzo Fernández, playing the pantomime villain after his role in England’s demise at the World Cup. Every Fernández touch was booed, although with Manchester City circling the bigger issue is whether the Argentina midfielder will play for Chelsea again.Everything will be clearer soon. Fulham had three chances to equalise but could not find the finish. Alonso has started well but there is more to come.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueFulhamChelseamatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Liverpool are still haunted by the mess of last summer | Liverpool | The Guardian
description: Sunday’s draw with Newcastle shows Andoni Iraola’s new ideas as manager will need to overcome the squad’s lack of balance
Author: Jonathan Wilson
Headline: Sunday’s draw with Newcastle shows Andoni Iraola’s new ideas as manager will need to overcome the squad’s lack of balance
Content: Virgil van Dijk, Ryan Gravenberch and Alexander Isak were part of Liverpool’s season-opening draw.Composite: Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenVirgil van Dijk, Ryan Gravenberch and Alexander Isak were part of Liverpool’s season-opening draw.Composite: Getty ImagesSoccer with Jonathan WilsonLiverpoolLiverpool are still haunted by the mess of last summerSunday’s draw with Newcastle shows Andoni Iraola’s new ideas as manager will need to overcome the squad’s lack of balanceSign up for our free newsletter hereJonathan WilsonMon 24 Aug 2026 11.42 EDTLast modified on Mon 24 Aug 2026 12.11 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe good news for Liverpool is that, Arsenal aside, every other team with vague title aspirations who played over the weekend looked undercooked, and that Andoni Iraola’s men did, in the end,come away from Newcastle with a point. But the vulnerability to the counter that undermined them so often last season has not gone away, and nor have they suddenly found a new creativity under Iraola.The main theme of the first three days of the new season was the value of stability. Manchester City under a new manager were poor and fortunateto overcome Bournemouth. Aston Villa, after big changes of players and backroom staff, werehammered at Brighton. Tottenham, midway through yet another overhaul, were dismal inlosing at Brentford. Manchester United at least provided a degree of stability by looking very much like the United of the past decade intheir defeat to Hull.Liverpool, for much of the first 96 minutes of their fixture at St James’ Park, looked like joining the list of challengers struggling to emerge from a summer of churn. Arne Slot spent much of last season complaining about how opponents always scored with their first chance and about Liverpool’s inability to deal with direct attacks, and as Anthony Elanga put Newcastle ahead, it seemed that not much had changed. Joe Willock’s goal to restore the Newcastle lead was much the same: opponents running at pace through vacant space.What is odd is how pressing the need for a replacement for Fabinho has been since the defensive midfielder left in 2023. Even as Liverpool won the league under Slot in 2024-25, the discussion was of how the squad needed of an overhaul, and how a dedicated holding player to operate alongside Ryan Gravenberch was a priority. Which was what made the spending spree of last summer so surprising: it wasn’t so much who came in as who didn’t.Without a holding midfielder, the flaws of the centre of defence, where Virgil van Dijk’s lack of pace on the turn is becoming increasingly obvious, are magnified. Liverpool could perhaps get away with it were he prepared to operate 10 yards higher in possession but the 35-year-old, aware of his ageing legs and worried about balls played in behind him, instinctively drops deeper, giving opponents just the sort of opportunities that Yoane Wissa kept exploiting on Sunday.Iraola insisted it wasn’t “just about personnel” – which itself seemed an implicit acknowledgment that it is in part about personnel. Had he scored, Iraola said, everybody would have praised Gravenberch, who had advanced to the edge of the Newcastle box in the attack that led to the first Liverpool concession. “I don’t want us to take that from his game but we have to adapt as a team to these situations,” said Iraola. “We have to know these situations can happen.”Of Newcastle’s second goal, he said: “It wasn’t like they caught us by surprise. We should compete for the first ball and probably make a foul – be a bit more aggressive against the ball carrier. There were different reasons for both the goals which happened in transition. We have been preparing in the week for these transitions but there’s a reason why Newcastle are so good at them. It’s not just because one person is playing there. It’s something we have to correct between a lot of players.”But conceding on the break isn’t the only familiar issue for Liverpool. Their full-backs, Jeremie Frimpong and Milos Kerkez, were unconvincing. Alexander Isak, booed throughout by the home fans, rarely looked dangerous in the first full 90 minutes he has completed since his British record transfer from Newcastle last summer. Florian Wirtz produced a characteristic performance full of neat touches and little incision.Iraola’s career suggests it often takes him time to instil his ideas at clubs. There is no reason for panic. Liverpool at least had the resilience to come back and pinch the draw. It’s not like any side other than Arsenal has looked particularly impressive. But perhaps there does need to be a reconsideration of what has gone before.The familiar narrative is that Slot drove the car that Jürgen Klopp had put together to a league title and was then found wanting. But while the Dutchman cannot escape blame for last season, an equally valid interpretation might be that Slot coaxed an ageing team to an unexpected league title. Then, with an overhaul badly needed – Jamie Carragher wasn’t alone in speaking towards the end of that season of Liverpool needing half a dozen new players – he was let down by those charged with recruitment.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Twice weeklySign up toSoccer DeskJonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionMichael Edwards left his role as chief executive for football at Fenway Sports Group, which owns Liverpool, in July, but the mess caused by last summer’s spree endures. Of the six most expensive signings of last summer for a combined fee of around £410m (about $560m), the only one who has looked remotely impressive, Hugo Ekitike, is still out for months with a ruptured achilles. Rarely has so much been spent in football to such destructive effect.This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US.Subscribe for free here.Explore more on these topicsLiverpoolSoccer with Jonathan WilsonPremier LeaguefeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Cycling chiefs criticised for response to Fin Tarling’s death: ‘This simply cannot happen’ | Cycling | The Guardian
description: Richard Plugge, the manager of the former Tour de France winner, Jonas Vingegaard, has criticised cycling’s governing body, the UCI, for a lack of action following the death of Fin Tarling
Author: Jeremy Whittle
Headline: Richard Plugge, the manager of the former Tour de France winner, Jonas Vingegaard, has criticised cycling’s governing body, the UCI, for a lack of action following the death of Fin Tarling
Content: Finlay Tarling competes in a race in France in May this year.Photograph: Abaca Press/Alamy Stock Photo/Alamy Live News.View image in fullscreenFinlay Tarling competes in a race in France in May this year.Photograph: Abaca Press/Alamy Stock Photo/Alamy Live News.CyclingCycling chiefs criticised for response to Fin Tarling’s death: ‘This simply cannot happen’Richard Plugge criticises UCI for its lack of action‘Riders must be certain they can race on a safe course’Jeremy WhittleMon 24 Aug 2026 10.17 EDTLast modified on Mon 24 Aug 2026 18.15 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRichard Plugge, the manager of the two-time Tour de France winner, Jonas Vingegaard, has criticised cycling’s governing body, the UCI, for a lack of action following the death of the teenage rider Fin Tarling 10 days ago and said cycling’s leading teams should take responsibility for ensuring safety in races.“Neither UCI president David Lappartient, nor anyone else, stands up and says: ‘Wait a minute, we really need to think about how we are going to prevent this from happening in the future,’” Plugge, the manager of the Vingegaard-led Visma-Lease a bike team, told the cycling website WielerFlits.Cyclists criticise ‘catastrophic’ safety measures after Finlay Tarling’s deathRead more“Maybe we as teams need to take responsibility for safety in races ourselves again. The lack of anger about what has happened is very disappointing to me.”The 19-year-old Tarling was killed during the Volta a Portugal when he was descending mid-race in pursuit of the peloton and collided with a non-race vehicle that was coming towards him on the race route, despite the road closure.“This boy encounters a car on a descent,” Plugge said of Tarling. “Can you imagine this happening during Formula One? That a car is suddenly driving on the track in the opposite direction? This actually does happen in a cycling race.“We are just carrying on. What disappoints me is that everyone says it is terrible, but then immediately a ‘but’ follows. We need to skip everything after the ‘but’. This simply cannot happen.”Jonathan Vaughters, the manager of the EF Education-EasyPost team, has called for a reduction in the number of races on the professional racing calendar.“The problem is lack of standards and oversight and the need to keep too many races that do not meet professional standards on the calendar,” he said.“There are many races running on too small a budget to be hosting a professional-level race. We don’t need 600 days of racing. How about 100 days of racing, all of which are safe?”While a formal investigation into Tarling’s death is now under way, neither the UCI nor the PortugueseCyclingFederation (FPC) have been willing to comment any further, particularly on media statements made by the Portuguese police (GNR) which confirmed that Tarling had been isolated and racing without a police escort.The FPC said: “As the organiser of the Volta a Portugal, we believe it would be neither appropriate nor responsible for us to speculate on matters that are currently being investigated by the competent authorities.”The UCI said: “As the circumstances surrounding the incident are still being established, we will not be commenting further at this stage.”Unlike Europe’s three Grand Tours, in France, Italy and Spain, the Portuguese race, like many other smaller events, operates a rolling road closure, which relies on secure policing at the front and back of the race convoy.Rolling road closures were highlighted again last week when the Australian rider Maeve Plouffe said that she hadnearly been hit by a carwhile racing in the Tour of Britain Women.“There is a hole in the system of rolling road closures,” the Association of Professional Cyclists president and former professional Adam Hansen told the Guardian. “We have to fix this.”Hansen added: “The most dangerous moments I had in a race did not result in a major incident. It was pure luck that I did not die sometimes. The organisers just think if nothing happened, it was fine.”Plugge argued that the serial failures to prioritise athlete safety meant that changes to the structure of many races had now become inevitable.“If cycling from A to B on public roads over 200km is no longer feasible, then we must ride laps of 15, 20, or 25km, provided those routes can be 100% secured. The riders must be certain that they can race on a safe course.”Explore more on these topicsCyclingnewsShareReuse this content

title: Enes Kanter Freedom ejected from WNBA game after confrontation with Natasha Cloud | WNBA | The Guardian
description: The former WNBA center had criticized the WNBA’s transgender policy, declaring himself eligible for the league’s draft as a publicity stunt.
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The former WNBA center had criticized the WNBA’s transgender policy, declaring himself eligible for the league’s draft as a publicity stunt.
Content: Enes Kanter Freedom and Natasha Cloud exchanged words after Cloud’s basket.Photograph: Michael Reaves/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenEnes Kanter Freedom and Natasha Cloud exchanged words after Cloud’s basket.Photograph: Michael Reaves/Getty ImagesWNBAEnes Kanter Freedom ejected from WNBA game after confrontation with Natasha CloudFormer NBA center criticized WNBA’s transgender policyCloud yelled and pointed in his direction after scoringAssociated PressSun 23 Aug 2026 23.18 EDTLast modified on Sun 23 Aug 2026 23.19 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFormer NBA center Enes Kanter Freedom was ejected from Sunday night’s Indiana Fever v Chicago SkyWNBAgame after he was confronted by Sky guard Natasha Cloud late in the third quarter.Freedom was sitting along the baseline. He had on a black shirt that read “WOMAN. Noun. Adult human female.”The Fever called for a time out after Cloud scored inside with 1:22 left in the third quarter. Cloud then did a chest bump with teammate Aicha Coulibaly before turning around and walking in Kanter’s direction.WNBA commissioner says ‘haters’ trying to stir up debate about trans athletes and leagueRead moreCloud, 34, started yelling and pointing at Kanter, 34, as she approached him. A standing Kanter held his arms out and took one step on the court as security and a handful of Sky players moved in between the two.“There was just a fan incident and the security handled it, and we’re just going to focus on the game,” Chicago forward Azura Stevens said after the Sky’s 113-90 loss.Chicago coach Tyler Marsh said Cloud was concerned about being a distraction for the team.“I told her she wasn’t,” Marsh said. “I told her that we all embrace her as someone that protects our team and protects people that need to be protected and so Tash is always going to stand on that, and we stand for Tash.”Freedom stopped near the basket to plead his case to security as he was escorted from the court area. He spun around while holding his shirt out and encouraged the crowd to respond as he walked toward the front lobby.He had a conversation with a group of police officers before departing Wintrust Arena.“I didn’t see it, we were talking about the next play in our huddle,” Indiana star Caitlin Clark said, “so I think that’s probably a question for Chicago.”Cloud met with team and league security after the game. She did not speak with the media.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Weekly for the 2026 WNBA seasonSign up toWNBA 30A limited run women’s basketball newsletter dedicated to the league’s historic 30th season.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe WNBA has been the subject of recent debates on whether transgender women – people assigned male at birth who transition to align with their gender identity – should be allowed to participate in the league. There has never been such a player in the WNBA.Although the league’s collective bargaining agreement says the WNBA is restricted to women, it contains no more specific language about gender identity or sex assigned at birth.Fever guard Sophie Cunningham said in an ESPN profile published last month that she was opposed to transgender girls and women competing in girls’ and women’s sports. Freedom and Royce White, another former NBA player, have declared themselves eligible for the WNBA draft, saying they identify as women.Asked if he had a message for Kanter, Marsh praised the league and its players.“If you come to a game you should probably come to enjoy the basketball,” he said, “and that seems pretty simple to me. I think these players deserve that and have earned that. Being a former basketball player, you should probably understand and feel that too.”Explore more on these topicsWNBATransgenderBasketballnewsShareReuse this content

title: Glaring weakness in goal remains but early signs Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea should be fun | Chelsea | The Guardian
description: The failure to replace Robert Sánchez remains a mystery but the new-look front three should buy time for the new manager’s principles to bed in
Author: Jonathan Wilson
Headline: The failure to replace Robert Sánchez remains a mystery but the new-look front three should buy time for the new manager’s principles to bed in
Content: Xabi Alonso can only have been impressed by Cole Palmer and his forward line, but Robert Sánchez remains a weak link.Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenXabi Alonso can only have been impressed by Cole Palmer and his forward line, but Robert Sánchez remains a weak link.Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesChelseaAnalysisGlaring weakness in goal remains but early signs Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea should be funJonathan Wilsonat Craven CottageThe failure to replace Robert Sánchez remains a mystery but the new-look front three should buy time for the new manager’s principles to bed inMon 24 Aug 2026 18.33 EDTLast modified on Mon 24 Aug 2026 18.52 EDTShareAfter a weekend on whichpretty much every potential challengerto Arsenal haddemonstrated their flaws, there was a sense, perhaps even a need, for Chelsea to emerge as a serious contender – if only to prevent the title race becoming a procession. And while they were far from flawless, there were at least some indications that they could mount some kind of challenge.They looked extremely dangerous in the final third, and Cole Palmer was involved in all threeChelseagoals, perhaps benefiting from a first summer off in three years. But they were rather less impressive through midfield or at the back, despite Josh Acheampong’s all-action performance, while goalkeeper remains the problem it has been since Thibaut Courtois left.Chelsea’s front three dazzle as they edge out Fulham in derby thrillerRead moreIt could easily have gone wrong: in the final quarter-hour; Antonee Robinson lofted an effort wide with Robert Sánchez off his line and Ryan Sessegnon smacked a shot from a narrow angle straight at the Spanish keeper. But neither opportunity was taken and so Chelsea got Xabi Alonso’s reign off to a winning start.At this stage, performances and learning the system are probably the most important thing, but if there is to be some sort of dart at the title, results matter if only to keep Chelsea somewhere near the race until the point at which Alonso’s principles are absorbed and they do find something close to top form.Perhaps what’s most striking, though, ishow different the approach isto Enzo Maresca’s. Where Maresca prioritised control to often stultifying effect, Alonso’s game is based on rapid turnovers and transition. It’ll probably settle down as his systems become deeper rooted but there was a sense of recklessness at times to their play. It was harum-scarum, end-to-end, thrilling stuff, which is all very well to watch, and may even come as a relief afterthe sterility of Marescaandthe shambles of Liam Rosenior, but may not be great for consistency or sustained runs of form.Alonso could hardly have dreamed of a quicker start, João Pedro putting Chelsea ahead after 31 seconds, matching the record for the quickest goal scored in the reign of a Premier League manager, David Unsworth’s goal – also against Fulham – inDavid Moyes’s first game in charge of Evertonin March 2002. João Pedro had scored eight goals in eight pre-season games; and this a player Maresca told not to focus on scoring goals shortly before he went on a run of seven games without a shot. That was a first indication of a forward line starting to show signs of an impressive understanding. All three combined for the third goal, Morgan Rogers flicking on for João Pedro who held the ball up for the overlapping Palmer to slip his shot cleverly between Bernd Leno’s legs.View image in fullscreenJoão Pedro (second from left), Cole Palmer (second from right) and Morgan Rogers (right) combined impressively on their first outing as Chelsea’s front three.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianAlonso’s first go at finding a pattern amid the legions of players assembled by BlueCo involved a midfield made up of two players who, despite being at Chelsea together for the past three years, had never previously been paired in the centre: Roméo Lavia and Reece James. It was not entirely by choice: Moisés Caicedo was left out as a precaution while Enzo Fernández remained on the bench until the 65th minute asManchester City continue their pursuit of him. And it didn’t entirely work. It may look a defensively robust pairing but there were long spells when Fulham had control of midfield.A feature of Alonso’s approach, and one of the reasons it takes time and commitment to learn – qualities that were notably lacking at Real Madrid – is that players can emerge in unexpected positions. Which doesn’t entirely explain how the right-sided centre-back Maxence Lacroix found himself running on to Palmer’s pass in theFulhambox but, having got there, he demonstrated great poise to skip around Jorge Cuenca and cut the ball back for Rogers to score his first Chelsea goal.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionYet for all that was new and positive, and for all that was raw and unintentionally exciting, there wasone glaring and inexplicably familiar failingfor Chelsea: in goal. Sánchez’s positioning seemed very strange for Fulham’s first goal, drilled in at his near post by Josh King (who also benefited from a bizarrely ineffectual attempt to track from Rogers), and while it was a far less glaring error, he pushed Timothy Castagne’s shot straight to Gonzalo García for Fulham’s second.Although Sánchez doesn’t perhaps quite deserve the negative reputation he has among certain Chelsea fans, he did make a league-high five errors leading to goals in 2024-25 and three last season. It remains mystifying that a clubthat signs wide forwards by the dozencontinues to refuse to invest in a top-class goalkeeper. That may yet hold Chelsea back.Generally, though, Alonso can be satisfied with his start: a win against Chelsea’s local rivals, an impressive display from Acheampong, a number of fluent interactions from his front three and plenty of signs of his system beginning to take hold, with a few obvious improvements to be made. And from the point of view of fans and casual observers, it looks like it should be fun.Explore more on these topicsChelseaXabi AlonsoFulhamPremier LeagueanalysisShareReuse this content

title: Manchester City agree £34m deal for Allan Elias as Nico González nears Newcastle move  | Transfer window | The Guardian
description: Manchester City have agreed a €37.5m plus €2.5m (£34m) deal for Palmeiras’s winger Allan Elias, with the club also in advanced negotiations to sell Nico González to Newcastle
Author: Jamie Jackson
Headline: Manchester City have agreed a €37.5m plus €2.5m (£34m) deal for Palmeiras’s winger Allan Elias, with the club also in advanced negotiations to sell Nico González to Newcastle
Content: The Palmeiras winger Allan Elias has made 96 appearances for the club.Photograph: César Olmedo/ReutersView image in fullscreenThe Palmeiras winger Allan Elias has made 96 appearances for the club.Photograph: César Olmedo/ReutersTransfer windowManchester City agree £34m deal for Allan Elias as Nico González nears Newcastle movePalmeiras winger’s arrival paves way for Savinho exitCity monitoring Liverpool forward Cody GakpoJamie JacksonandLouise TaylorMon 24 Aug 2026 15.56 EDTLast modified on Mon 24 Aug 2026 18.27 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleManchester City have agreed a €37.5m plus €2.5m (£34m) deal for the Palmeiras winger Allan Elias, with the club also in advanced negotiations to sell Nico González to Newcastle.The 22-year-old Elias – known as Allan – made his senior debut for Palmeiras last year and has made 96 appearances for the club, scoring nine goals and making 12 assists. He is yet to play for Brazil.Post-Pep Premier League era begins with blast of hyper-managed shock and awe | Barney RonayRead moreAllan’s arrival will clear the way for the sale of his countryman Savinho to Tottenham for £75m plus £10m. Spurs also want to sign City’s Omar Marmoush, with the fee for the forward expected to be £75m. While Savinho has informed Enzo Maresca he wishes to leave, City’s manager said on Friday that the Egyptian had not done so.González is expected to be sold to Newcastle for a fee in the region of £50m, a price almost identical to the £49.8m City paid Porto for the midfielder in the January 2025 window. Newcastle are understood to be confident of signing the 24-year-old.The money from his proposed sale may be used by City to make an official bid for Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández. While Chelsea set a deadline for any offer for the midfielder of 14 August, which was not met, City may test their resolve, as the player is open to a move and a reunion with his former coach Maresca.Quick GuidePlay our football trivia game, On the ballShowThe Guardian'sdaily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues?Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.City have so far made only one senior signing in the window, the £116m purchase of Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest, but are close to sealing the €95m (£81.4m) plus €5m deal for Ayyoub Bouaddi. The Lille midfielder is thought to have undergone his medical on Monday.City are also thought to retain an interest in Liverpool’s wide forward Cody Gakpo with Spurs also closely monitoring the Dutchman’s availability. IfLiverpoolsign Bradley Barcola and another winger, they may be open to Gakpo’s departure. Liverpool are pondering a third bid for Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh while they continue to talk with Paris Saint-Germain over Ibrahim Mbaye and Barcola.Explore more on these topicsTransfer windowManchester CityLiverpoolNewcastle UnitednewsShareReuse this content

title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 4: Brighton | Brighton & Hove Albion Women | The Guardian
description: Dario Vidosic has added nous and potential in a bid to build on a season that saw the club get to a first FA Cup final
Author: Sophie Downey
Headline: Dario Vidosic has added nous and potential in a bid to build on a season that saw the club get to a first FA Cup final
Content: Brighton were one of only three teams to beat the champions Manchester City last season. Photograph: Steve Bardens/Getty ImagesDario Vidosic has added nous and potential in a bid to build on a season that saw the club get to a first FA Cup finalBySophie DowneyMon 24 Aug 2026 19.01 EDTLast modified on Mon 24 Aug 2026 20.01 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleGuardian writers’ predicted position:6th (NB: this is not necessarily Sophie Downey’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)Last season’s position:7thProspectsAfirst FA Cup finalwas a historic moment for Brighton. Despitelosing to Manchester Cityat Wembley, it will have filled Dario Vidosic and his team with the belief that they are on the right track.It has been a summer of relative stability on the south coast. While there are seven new faces, departures have been limited to four. The arrivals of Lia Wälti and Gabby George bring vast experience and increased defensive acumen to the ranks while the Republic of Ireland’s Emily Murphy and Poland’s Nadia Krezyman are young attacking talents who have started to make a name for themselves.Brighton’s Emilie Joramo: ‘I feel like I’m now in the place I want to be’Read moreBrighton’s inconsistency was their downfall last season. They were seriously hampered by the lack of an out-and-out centre-forward after the anterior cruciate ligament injury suffered by the Arsenal loanee and England Euros hero Michelle Agyemang. Kiko Seike finished as their highest scorer in the league with eight and she was their only representative in the Women’s Super League’s top 20 for goals and assists. That problem remains unsolved and will surely be a focus for the remainder of the transfer window.The conclusion of their season certainly gave Brighton something to build on over the summer. They secured an impressive league victoryover Cityanda draw against Arsenaland will hope to outdo the latter when they host Renée Slegers’s sideat Crawley in their opener on 6 September. That on paper is the toughest of Brighton’s opening four fixtures.A graph showing where Brighton have finished in the WSL over the past five seasons: 7th in 2022, 11th in 2023, 9th in 2024, 5th in 2025, 7th in 2026Off-field picturePinterest has become the first solo sponsor of the women’s team with a four-year partnership. The deal pivots around the concept of ‘matchday style’, bringing to life the way fans show support for their team. Plans continue for the construction ofEurope’s first purpose-built women’s football stadium. Located next to the Amex Stadium, the hope is it will open for the start of the 2030-2031 campaign.The managerNow entering his third season, Vidosic is the second-longest serving manager in the WSL, a period that has brought much-needed stability to the club and allowed the Croatian-born Australian time to fully implement his aggressive pressing and possession-based style.He has been on a journey, developing an out-of-possession style to help his team deal with some of the bigger clubs in the WSL The 39-year-old has never hidden from his desire to bring silverware to Brighton and last season’s FA Cup final will have given him a taste of the steps required to realise that ambition.Star signingThe acquisition of Wälti remains one of the biggest coups of the summer. The 33-year-old Switzerland captain returns to England after a year in Italy with Juventus, bringing with her a wealth of experienceand, from her seven years with Arsenal, a WSL title and a Champions League winners’ medal. Wälti’s technical ability is second-to-none, as is a level of intelligence that allows her to dictate play from the middle of the park. She leads by example and guided Switzerland to the quarter-finals at Euro 2025. If Wälti can stay injury-free, she could play a significant role this season.View image in fullscreenLia Wälti should bring quality and know-how to Brighton.Photograph: Neil Holmes/Focus Images Ltd/ShutterstockStat attackBrighton had a finishing problem in 2025-26. Not in terms of hitting the target – no other side had as strong a shot accuracy – but only three teams converted a lower proportion of their on-target efforts. If the Seagulls can fire towards the corners of the goal rather than close to the goalkeeper, they could fly this season.A graphic showing that last season Brighton had the highest percentage of shots on target in the league, but the fourth-worst conversion of shots on target to goalsSet for a breakthroughSophie Peskett has already made history when in 2021, aged 18, she became Ipswich’s first professional player. The winger spent the best part of seven years at Ipswich, making 127 appearances and helping them earn promotion to the WSL 2 twice. Now 23, it would have been a big decision for her to leave, but Brighton seems like a sensible next step. A nifty player with an eye for goal, Peskett will prove useful to Brighton’s attacking output.What they say …“Brighton is not a team that has to hide. In the last couple of years, they’ve been able to hurt the big teams in many moments, and they reached the FA Cup final last season as well. We’re not going to be favourites in every single game, but that’s a nice position to be in.”– Lia WältiWhere are they playing their home games?Brighton will continue to play most of their home games at Crawley’s Broadfield Stadium although four of their six opening home fixtures will be at the Amex. The club have added an Amex 4-Match Pack to their ticketing options, priced at £45 for adults. The club have also launched ‘Built For Her’, their dedicated women’s football membership option that offers a bundle of exclusive perks as they look to build their fanbase before the stadium move.Explore more on these topicsWSL season previews 2026-27Brighton & Hove Albion WomenWomen's Super LeagueWomen's footballfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Nottingham Forest close in on signing Liam Delap from Chelsea | Transfer window | The Guardian
description: Liam Delap is nearing a move to Nottingham Forest from Chelsea, with the two clubs in advanced talks
Author: Ben Fisher
Headline: Liam Delap is nearing a move to Nottingham Forest from Chelsea, with the two clubs in advanced talks
Content: Liam Delap has not been involved in first-team training at Chelsea.Photograph: VCG/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenLiam Delap has not been involved in first-team training at Chelsea.Photograph: VCG/Getty ImagesTransfer windowNottingham Forest close in on signing Liam Delap from ChelseaOliver Glasner wants two more buys in transfer windowAston Villa target Club Brugge defender Joel OrdóñezBen FisherMon 24 Aug 2026 17.31 EDTLast modified on Mon 24 Aug 2026 17.35 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleNottingham Forest are in advanced talks with Chelsea over a deal for Liam Delap. Oliver Glasner wants two more signings before the transfer window closes a week on Tuesday.Delap, who was on Forest’s radar when the striker opted to joinChelseafrom Ipswich, is out of favour at Stamford Bridge and has been training away from Xabi Alonso’s first team. The 23-year-old was left out of Chelsea’s squad for their game at Fulham on Monday.Manchester City agree £34m deal for Allan Elias as Nico González nears Newcastle moveRead moreGlasner, who has implemented a three-man defence at Forest, is also keen to strengthen at wing-back. “The club is working very hard to get these deals done,” the Austrian head coach said. “I’m very confident that we will get in two more high-quality players.”Forest have signed Ousmane Diomande, Xaver Schlager and Steven Benda this summer, paying a fee only for the former. Diomande joined in a £34m deal from Sporting. Forest host Leeds in the Carabao Cup second round on Tuesday, a rematch of their Premier League defeat last Saturday. Morgan Gibbs-White will miss the game because of a knee problem but Forest hope he will available for the trip to Liverpool on Saturday.Quick GuidePlay our football trivia game, On the ballShowThe Guardian'sdaily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues?Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Elsewhere,Aston Villaare ramping up their interest in the Club Brugge defender Joel Ordóñez. Villa want the Ecuador centre-back, a longstanding target who impressed against them in the Champions League, to replace Ezri Konsa. Villa had a bid for Southampton’s Taylor Harwood-Bellis rejected.Coventry City are working on a deal to make the Brentford defender Ethan Pinnock their ninth summer signing. The 33-year-old, who joined from Barnsley in 2019, made just four top-flight appearances last season.
